summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted with worsening cough, green sputum, subjective fever, and hypoxemia. He was initially uncooperative in the ED but became alert and oriented on admission, though tremulous. He reported heavy alcohol use, last drink 12 hours prior, and symptoms consistent with alcohol withdrawal. Labs showed hypernatremia, which improved with IV fluids. A chest X-ray revealed new lung opacities suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with levofloxacin, metronidazole, prednisone, and nebulizers for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia, and diazepam for alcohol withdrawal. Hypertension was managed with amlodipine. Despite clinical improvement, he eloped from the hospital on the third day before completing treatment or receiving discharge instructions.
